description: Topic probes for a discovery pass. Each is measured with WORD BOUNDARIES against both the local corpus and the surveyed market text. A probe may declare which kinds it applies to; a probe with no kinds applies to all of them. Supply your own; these found real gaps in a real curriculum and are kept as a worked example.
probeDesignRules: MEASURE THE SUBJECT, NOT ITS PROPER NOUNS. A regex that is a list of product names measures vocabulary, not coverage. Ours claimed we taught nothing about agent orchestration because we never write 'LangChain'; we had a nine-module class-ready path on it.

REJECT GENERIC WORDS THAT HAVE A SECOND MEANING. '\badapters?\b' looks like a fine-tuning term and matched 134 software-integration adapters, reporting a real gap as covered. A hidden gap is worse than a false one: nobody goes looking for it.

THE CORPUS IS JSON, SO FIELD NAMES ARE IN THE TEXT. '\bnarration\b' matched 333 instances of "kind":"narration", an asset cue type, not a single word of subject matter. Check what a term matches before trusting its count.

DO NOT BROADEN INTO AN ADJACENT CONCEPT. 'grounded answer' is the outcome of retrieval-augmented generation, not the technique. Folding it into the RAG probe would hide the gap the same way 'adapters' did.

A PRODUCT NAME IS A MOVING TARGET. When a proper noun genuinely is the subject, probe every name the product has held. 'Azure AI Foundry' scores 0 and 0, which reads as a total gap; the product was renamed, and 'Microsoft Foundry' scores 1 and 9. A regex pinned to a retired name reports absence and is believed.
AFTER EDITING A REGEX, RUN --offline AND READ THE COUNTS. Every failure above exited 0 and looked healthy.

probes.title: Retrieval-augmented generation, embeddings, and vector search
probes.audited: 2026-08-03. Kept narrow deliberately. Broadening with 'grounded answer' scores 4 in Learn and would erase the gap, but grounding is the outcome, not the retrieval technique. Do not add it.

probes.title: Embeddings and vector stores
probes.audited: 2026-08-03. Subject terms, no second meaning. Unchanged.

probes.title: Agent orchestration and multi-agent patterns
probes.audited: 2026-08-03. REPLACES the old orchestration-frameworks probe, which searched only for LangChain, LlamaIndex and Semantic Kernel. Those appear zero times, so it reported a nine-module class-ready path as a total gap. This regex measures the subject and scores 81 in Learn, 27 in Field Guide.

probes.title: Mapping our orchestration patterns onto named frameworks
probes.audited: 2026-08-03. NEW. The proper nouns are still worth measuring, but as what they actually are: a vocabulary bridge. We teach orchestration entirely in our own terms, so a reader who knows LangChain cannot tell that our material covers what they need. That is a portability gap, not a coverage gap, and it is one bridging piece rather than a curriculum.

probes.title: AI for executives, leaders, and decision makers
probes.audited: 2026-08-03. Broadened from executives/board-level to include decision maker and C-suite. Still scores 1 in Learn and 0 in Field Guide, so the gap is real and survives the broadening.

probes.title: Fine-tuning, adapters, distillation, and when not to train
probes.audited: 2026-08-03. FIXED TWO WAYS. The old regex never searched for 'fine-tun' at all despite the id, and its bare '\badapters?\b' matched 134 software-integration adapters in Learn and 38 in Field Guide, reporting the topic as covered. Real counts are 5 in Learn and 0 in Field Guide. This probe was hiding a gap, which is the more dangerous direction of the same error.

probes.title: Voice agents, virtual instructors, and accessible media
probes.audited: 2026-08-03. Added TTS, STT and virtual instructor, all of which score 0, so the gap holds. DELIBERATELY EXCLUDES 'narration' and 'caption': narration alone scores 333 in Learn, every one of them the JSON asset cue "kind":"narration", and captions appear only as an accessibility requirement. Neither is subject matter. Do not add them.

probes.title: Model Context Protocol and tool interoperability
probes.audited: 2026-08-03. A proper noun, but here the proper noun IS the subject. Correctly reported Learn and Field Guide as covered and the visual guide as absent, which holds up: no diagram file mentions MCP.

probes.title: Prompt injection and untrusted content handling
Cost, capacity, and spend control for AI systems
probes.audited: 2026-08-03. Added TPM and spend limit. Kept scoped to cost CONTROL on purpose: bare 'cost' appears 355 times because we discuss cost constantly, while the mechanisms for capping it are what is missing.

probes.title: Managed model platforms, and choosing between hosting and self-hosting
probes.audited: 2026-08-03. NEW. Measures the SUBJECT, not a vendor. Scores 3 in Learn and 0 in Field Guide against 21 and 38 for self-hosting, so the curriculum teaches one side of a two-sided decision. Deliberately NOT broadened to bare 'hosted', which scores 39 and 39 because it also matches every instance of self-hosted. Related finding worth its own piece later: rival platform names (Bedrock, Vertex AI, SageMaker, Azure ML) score 0 and 0, so we name no managed platform at all. That is a vocabulary bridge like orchestration-framework-portability, not a coverage gap.

probes.title: Microsoft Foundry, from provisioning to model deployment
probes.audited: 2026-08-03. NEW, and it corrects a claim made without measuring. The reported finding was that Azure AI Foundry scores 0 in Learn and 0 in Field Guide, therefore we teach it not at all. Both zeros are real and both are misleading: the product was RENAMED, and 'Microsoft Foundry' scores 1 in Learn and 9 in Field Guide. This regex carries both names plus Foundry used as the platform noun, and scores 1 and 11. The gap is therefore narrow and one-sided rather than total: the Field Guide already carries decision-grade coverage in model-provider-decisions, while Learn has a single mention and no module.
